10.0.s.en: (1) The killing of the house of Ahab

10.0.0.en: Ahab had seventy sons, meaning sons and grandsons, who perhaps had taken refuge in Samaria, the fortified city, and sheltered in it from Jehu. Perhaps the rulers of Israel also took refuge in Samaria to escape from the face of Jehu, so Jehu sent to them, because they had authority in the city, and also because he wanted to share the responsibility with Ahab's guardians, that is, the guardians who cared for the sons and grandsons of Ahab and had a great standing with them. Jehu sent to address them so that he might be able to do away with the sons of Ahab.

10.1.0.en: Jehu sent to the officials in Samaria mentioned above, provoking them and testing them, whether they were subject to him or not. He told them in the letter that, since you have with you:

10.1.1.en: 1- the sons of your master Ahab, the former king;

10.1.2.en: 2- chariots and horses, which are the most important equipment in war;

10.1.3.en: 3- your city Samaria, fortified with high walls and strong trumpets;

10.1.5.en: then choose the best of your master's sons and set him on the throne in Samaria.

10.1.6.en: If they were rebellious, they would not answer the letter, and then he would attack them. And if they were subject to him and afraid of him, he could get rid, through them, of his enemies, who are all the descendants of Ahab and whoever is connected with him by kinship, or his supporters.

10.2.0.en: The rulers of Jezreel who lived in Samaria, and likewise the guardians responsible for Ahab's descendants, were very afraid of Jehu's letter, because he had killed two kings, Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah, so how could they stand before him? Especially as they were troubled by having no leader, after the death of Jehoram. They were accustomed to obeying a leader, not to leading the kingdom.

10.3.0.en: After the alarm and terror of the rulers of the city of Samaria, who were the one in charge of the city, the one in charge of the royal palace, and likewise the elders of the city and the guardians of Ahab's descendants, they wrote a letter in which they showed their complete submission to Jehu and to all his commands, and declared to him their refusal to set up a king from the descendants of Ahab.

10.4.0.en: The city of Jezreel: the most important city of the plain of Jezreel, which lies in the middle of the kingdom of Israel and extends from the river Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea. This city is located southwest of Hebron, at a distance of six miles.

10.4.1.en: After the letter of the rulers of the city reached Jehu and he learned of their submission to him, he sent them a second letter in which he said that the proof of your submission to me is that you come to me tomorrow with the heads of the seventy men, the sons of Ahab. He did not give them a chance to think, but in their fear and panic he commanded them to kill the sons of their master. Of course the killing of Ahab's sons by the guardians shows their evil and their disloyalty to the house of Ahab and their sharing in this hideous massacre, so they are Jehu's partners in this brutality and evil. Here Jehu's political shrewdness appears in making the rulers of Samaria kill the sons of Ahab, so that it would appear before all the people of Israel that he was not the killer of the house of Ahab but the rulers of Samaria were, and so the people would not be stirred up against him.

10.5.0.en: When the letter came to the elders of the city, they carried out Jehu's request, so they killed seventy men, the sons of Ahab, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezreel, where he was staying. It is noted that the elders of Samaria did not go to Jehu themselves, for fear of him, but they obeyed his word, killed the sons of Ahab and sent their heads to him, as clear proof that they had killed them and not any other people.

10.6.0.en: One of Jehu's servants came and told him of the arrival of the severed heads of the king's sons, and he commanded that they be put in two heaps at the entrance of the gate of the city until morning. Jehu put them at the entrance of the city so that all who entered Jezreel or left it would see them and fear Jehu and submit to him, and so that the news would spread throughout Israel and all the people would fear him.

10.7.0.en: In the morning the people of Jezreel gathered around the two heaps of skulls, and Jehu went out to them and proudly declared that he had been able to rebel against his master King Jehoram, and even kill him. But craftily he declared his innocence of killing the sons of Ahab, asking who had killed them! Although it was he who had commanded the elders of Samaria to kill them. He is crafty and politically shrewd, and the truth is that he is a beast and a liar.

10.8.0.en: Jehu hid his brutality and crimes behind God's command to Elijah that He would destroy the descendants of Ahab, in order to show himself submissive to God and carrying out His commands, and so win the people to himself. Truly he fulfilled Elijah's prophecy, but he fulfilled it with brutality, because he was wicked and fierce, so he deserved God's wrath, as we shall see at the end of the chapter.

10.9.0.en: Jehu was not content with doing away with the sons of Ahab, but also killed all the members of his large family who lived in Jezreel, as well as all his helpers in government and all his friends and his priests, until none of them was left alive.

10.9.1.en: Jehu followed the course of one who justifies his actions, clothing them with zeal for the Lord and His law, while in truth he was seeking to satisfy his lust for power and the subjection of others. So do not deceive others and cover your sins with verses and teachings of the Church, because justifying faults angers God greatly and keeps you from repentance, and nothing awaits you but destruction.

10.10.s.en: (2) The killing of the brethren of Ahaziah

10.10.0.en: Beth-eked of the shepherds: a town between Jezreel and Samaria. It is present-day Beit Qad, and is also called, for short, "Beth-eked," and it is the place where the shepherds tie up their sheep until they shear them.

10.10.1.en: The brethren of Ahaziah: the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah are meant (2 Chr 22:8), because Ahaziah's brethren had died (2 Chr 21:17). After Jehu finished killing everyone in Jezreel who had a connection with Ahab, he arose and headed for Samaria, and as he passed by "Beth-eked of the shepherds," he met a group of men and asked them who they were, and they told him that they were the brethren of King Ahaziah, and that they were on their way to visit the children of Ahab and his wife Jezebel, for they did not know that Jehu had killed the whole house of Ahab.

10.11.0.en: Jehu commanded that the brethren of Ahaziah be seized and killed, and they were forty-two men, and this was at the pit of Beth-eked, and perhaps he threw their bodies into this pit.

10.11.1.en: Do not be violent in your dealings with others, or rejoice that they dread you and fear you, for you are responsible to be a light to the world and salt of the earth, and whatever your authority, be humble and loving to those around you and show it to them. And if you are firm in some situations, do not lose your kindness toward those around you.

10.12.s.en: (3) The agreement with Jehonadab the son of Rechab

10.12.0.en: Jehonadab the son of Rechab: he was the leader of the Rechabites, who were of the descendants of the Kenites. They had lived with the children of Israel when they entered the land of Canaan, and they do not follow the creed of the Jews but have their own way of life, which is distinguished by the following:

10.12.1.en: 1- Abstaining from drinking wine and from planting vineyards, which could lead to the production of wine.

10.12.2.en: 2- Dwelling in tents and not building houses, because of their being strangers to the world, like the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

10.12.3.en: 3- Abstaining from farming, so as not to become attached to the crops they harvest, but to rely on God and work by herding.

10.12.4.en: Jeremiah mentioned them clearly (Jer 35). Jehu went out from Jezreel headed for Samaria, and on the way he found Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming out to meet him, and Jehu asked him, "Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart?" He meant, are you with me and loyal to me, as I am with you and accept you? Jehonadab answered, confirming his agreement with Jehu. Jehonadab agreed with him in the worship of God and the rejection of evil, whereas Jehu meant Jehonadab's loyalty to him personally, regardless of God. Jehonadab loved Jehu because he removed the evils of Ahab, while Jehu fulfilled the will of God but with brutality and for his personal interests. Jehonadab came out to meet Jehu to declare to him his support for him in removing evil.

10.12.5.en: Then Jehu stretched out his hand to Jehonadab and shook his hand, declaring their agreement together, and then helped him up into his chariot, that is, to sit beside Jehu, so that all would see Jehonadab's agreement with and support of Jehu by his sitting beside him in the chariot.

10.12.6.en: The commitment of the Rechabites, which continued until the time of the writing of this book and extended three hundred years, to the days of Jeremiah, inspires us to commit to God's commandments, however heavy they may seem, out of our love for Him, because He loved us first and gave His life for us on the Cross. And when we keep His commandments, He too is committed to our salvation and to granting us peace in our hearts. The commitment of the Rechabites to the teachings of their leader increased when they saw evil increase in the kingdom of Israel, so instead of adapting and becoming lax under the influence of those around them, they became more committed. So stand firm in holding to God's commandments, however much evil increases around you.

10.13.0.en: Jehu said to Jehonadab, "Come with me, and see my zeal for the LORD." So he took him with him in the same chariot. Jehu's words show his pride and his love of display in showing his zeal, in addition to the fact that his zeal was against the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal and not against the worship of idols as a whole, for he continued in the worship of the calves that Jeroboam had set up (v. 29).

10.14.0.en: When Jehu reached Samaria, he destroyed all who were left of Ahab's supporters, thereby fulfilling the Lord's sentence which He spoke to Elijah. We notice that in his destruction of evil two faults appeared in Jehu:

10.14.1.en: 1- He was concerned to gather supporters for himself, to show his power in pride and not for the glory of God, and he did not rely on the power of God but on material power, because his faith in God was weak.

10.14.2.en: 2- He did not turn to Elisha the man of God, who was present at that time, because he did not care about submitting to God.

10.15.s.en: (4) The killing of the priests of Baal

10.15.0.en: Jehu used a trick to be able to gather the priests of Baal in one place so as to do away with them easily. In a speech before the people he spread the word that he would worship Baal with more sincerity than Ahab had done. What is meant by saying that Ahab served Baal a little is that Ahab halted between two opinions, serving Baal at times and then declaring that he worshiped God at other times.

10.16.0.en: All his worshipers: everyone who cares about the worship of Baal.

10.16.1.en: Jehu showed his concern for the worship of Baal by announcing the offering of a great sacrifice to Baal, calling all the prophets of Baal and his priests and those who worship him to attend the rites of offering the sacrifice, and that no one should be absent, for whoever was absent would be killed. This was a great trick of Jehu in order to do away with the worshipers of Baal; he wanted to gather all the supporters of Baal by stressing that anyone who did not come would be killed, so as to ensure the destruction of Baal worship, so that no one would escape and set up worship of Baal anywhere in Israel.

10.17.0.en: Solemn assembly: a day set apart for worship (Lev 23:26-33). To carry his trick further, he proclaimed that a solemn assembly must be kept, as a sanctification of the soul, before the feast of the sacrifice, and this call was proclaimed. None of the worshipers of Baal objected, for fear of Jehu.

10.18.0.en: Jehu summoned all the worshipers of Baal from all over Israel, and no one was left behind, and they entered the temple of Baal, and filled it from end to end.

10.19.0.en: Jehu commanded the man in charge of the wardrobe to bring out vestments for all the worshipers of Baal, and he did so, for the worshipers of Baal used to take off their clothes and put on special clothes for worship. And because the number of the worshipers of Baal was large and not all of them had brought worship garments, Jehu brought out for them the worship garments from the treasury of the temple. His apparent purpose was to sanctify the worship of Baal by these special garments, but his hidden purpose was to distinguish the worshipers of Baal from others so as to make it easy to kill them.

10.20.0.en: Jehu went in, accompanied by Jehonadab the son of Rechab, to the house of Baal and called to those inside, asking them to make sure of those present, lest there be among them any who worshiped the Lord, but only the worshipers of Baal. Jehonadab did not take part in Jehu's deceit and lie but appeared here only with Jehu to make sure that none of the worshipers of the Lord was there, so that he would not be exposed to death, because Jehu had told Jehonadab his plan when he rode with him in the chariot.

10.21.0.en: The rites of offering the sacrifice began, and all went in to offer it to their god Baal. Jehu had set an ambush of eighty men around the temple and charged them that none of the worshipers of Baal should escape, and warned them that their lives would be in place of the lives of any who escaped their hands, for they were to seize and kill any of the worshipers of Baal who tried to flee.

10.22.1.en: Captains (thirds): those with military ranks, that is, officers.

10.22.2.en: After the priests of Baal finished offering their sacrifices and the hearts of all the worshipers were attached to Baal, Jehu commanded the guards under him to attack the temple and kill everyone in it, and they killed them all and threw their bodies on the ground. Then they went to the city of Baal, a group of buildings in which the priests of Baal lived, and brought out all the wooden images of the house of Baal and burned them.

10.23.0.en: They broke down the image of Baal and tore down his temple and turned it into a dunghill, as a sign of its defilement and contempt, and it remained so until the day of the writing of this book. In this Jehu did away with the worship of Baal in Israel.

10.23.1.en: May you despise and reject everything connected with evil and trample it under your feet, that your heart may be free for the worship and love of God, because God cannot agree with the evils of the world.

10.24.0.en: But Jehu did not turn completely from idolatry to serve God alone, for he kept Jeroboam's two golden calves, which were in Bethel and in Dan (1 Kgs 12:25-33), which were a national religion in Israel and had become, according to the prevailing custom, recognized.

10.25.0.en: The Lord rewarded Jehu for his role in carrying out God's judgment on the house of Ahab, which was a just judgment on Ahab's evils and bad deeds, by letting Jehu's sons sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

10.25.1.en: God's rewarding of Jehu does not mean His approval of his brutality or pride, but He rewards him only for removing the evil of Ahab. This material reward, the sitting of his sons on the throne of the kingdom of Israel to the fourth generation, does not mean the salvation of his soul or his entering the Kingdom, but He gives him an earthly reward in return for his work.

10.26.0.en: But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord with all his heart, for he continued to commit the sins of Jeroboam, who led Israel after him into transgression and made them sin, that is, he continued in the worship of idols.

10.27.0.en: In those days: that is, in the days of Jehu's reign.

10.27.1.en: To cut short (to cut off): to take and cut off lands and cities from the kingdom of Israel and give them to the Gentiles. This is a chastisement and punishment from God upon Israel.

10.27.2.en: During Jehu's life, the surrounding kingdoms were cutting off parts of his kingdom from every side, especially in the territories of the tribes east of the Jordan, which are fertile lands, for the Lord used Hazael as a rod with which to strike Jehu. This was a judgment from God on his conduct.

10.27.3.en: If God allows trials to come to you, they are a chastisement to remind you of your sins so that you repent, and not a rejection of you by God. So do not murmur or despair, but return to God, for He is your Father and loves you, and He wipes away all evil from you, and you regain your sonship in Him.

10.28.0.en: Aroer: a town to the north of the river Arnon.

10.28.1.en: The valley of Arnon: the Arnon is a river called today "Wadi al-Mujib," in the Kingdom of Jordan, and it flows into the Dead Sea.

10.28.2.en: Gilead: a mountainous region east of the Jordan, which includes modern Balqa.

10.28.3.en: Bashan: a province in the land of Canaan, east of the Jordan, between the mountains of Hermon and Gilead.

10.28.4.en: Hazael struck the children of Israel in all their coasts (borders), beginning from the east of the Jordan, including the land of Gilead and the lands of the Gadites, the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is in the valley of Arnon, and Gilead and Bashan.

10.29.0.en: As for the rest of the acts of Jehu and all that he did, they were recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel, which is different from the book of Chronicles that is in the Holy Bible.

10.30.0.en: Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz succeeded him on the throne of Israel.

10.31.0.en: The reign of Jehu over Israel in Samaria lasted twenty-eight years.

10.31.1.en: He reigned a long time, and none reigned longer than he except his grandson Jeroboam II, who reigned forty-one years (ch. 14:23). Athaliah, then Joash, reign over Judah
